newsitem.title: INDIA: Bank Am urges Indian importers to hedge positions.
newsitem.headline: Bank Am urges Indian importers to hedge positions.

text.p: Indian importers should take advantage of the prevailing spot and forward dollar rates to hedge their positions, the head of Indian forex operations at Bank of America said on Monday.

"I think importers should relook their positions and avail of the opportunity of a lower spot rate and low forward premium to hedge their positions," Arun Dobe, Bank of America's forex director told Reuters.
The spot rupee was trading at 35.76/77 against the dollar late Monday morning compared to a broad 35.80 to 35.90 range at which it has traded for most of the last six months.
The six month annualised forward premium closed at 4.47 percent on Friday, a very attractive rate for importers to cover their forward positions.
But most importers have been leaving their positions uncovered, given the firmness of the rupee in recent months and on expectations it will remain firm in the near term.
"Current call money rates of 0.25 percent to 1.0 percent (for overnight money) are likely to go up and importers will lose an opportunity when the premiums rise," Dobe said.
He said the advice applied also to Indian firms which borrowed in dollars from FCNR (B) (foreign currency non-resident) accounts and sold them outright in the local market.
